h1: Slip rolls — motorized sheet metal rollers
intro: Slip rollers for HVAC, sign, ducting and general sheet-metal shops: three rolls, a drop-end to slip the finished cylinder off and wire grooves at the roll ends for wired edges. İşitan's IR series is the motorized slip roll — 3.4 ft to 6.7 ft floor-standing machines up to 14 ga, with foot pedal and brake motor for daily use — and the RST-M is the reinforced economical motorized roll. Sold with CSA-approved panels and supported from Mississauga, ON.

groups.title: Motorized slip rolls and economical plate rollers
groups.lead: The IR motorized slip rolls and the economical RST-M — the light-gauge rolls of the sheet-metal shop.

faq.q: What is the difference between a slip roll and a plate roller?
faq.a: They work the same way — three rolls that pinch and bend the sheet — but a slip roll is built for thin sheet (up to about 14 ga) and the top roll "slips" out of its bearing so the finished cylinder can be removed; its wire grooves also form wired edges. Plate rollers have larger rolls, heavier frames and powered or hydraulic roll positioning for plate from 11 ga up to 1/2″ and beyond.

The IR is the daily-use slip roll: both rolls driven through a gearbox, a brake motor that stops the rolls exactly where the operator wants them, a geared lock for quick back-roll adjustment and ten sizes from 3.4 to 6.7 ft. The RST-M is the value-priced roll for light ducting and signage work in 12 ga and thinner, with the back and bottom rolls set by screws.

faq.q: What do the wire grooves do?
faq.a: The grooves at the end of the rolls (3/16″, 1/4″ and 3/8″ on most models) close a hemmed edge around a wire to make a stiff, safe wired edge on ducts, buckets and tanks.

faq.q: What voltage do İşitan plate rollers run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor.
